intent: Restructure the docs pack into frontend, backend and database layer folders and make the agent setup harness-neutral (Claude Code + Hermes) with ECC and graphify.
summary: Split the single frontend, backend, RBAC, PWA and Google docs into three layer folders (frontend-architecture/, backend-architecture/, database-architecture/) plus system-overview.md, keeping the content and remapping every cross-reference. Added agent-operations/ (Claude Code as default builder, Hermes Agent as default operator, ECC per harness, handoffs, coordination rules), a generated .hermes.md via scripts/agent-context.ts because Hermes loads one context file and ignores @ imports, graphify install and always-on steps for both harnesses, and a provider-agnostic LLM layer so the product can use Claude or Hermes models. The contract moved to v1.1 (C-19 precedence, C-20 memories are not facts, agent configuration behind the human gate). Added tasks PSI-009 and PSI-095 to PSI-098 and updated existing task criteria to the new paths. Nothing is committed to a repository yet, so PSI-003 is still not done.

decisions.decision: Separate database-architecture/ next to backend-architecture/ instead of one backend folder
decisions.reason: With Supabase most backend logic and all authorization are SQL, which has its own change rules (immutable migrations), review gates and tests (pgTAP)
alternatives: database/ as a subfolder of backend-architecture/

decisions.decision: Claude Code is the default builder and Hermes Agent the default operator, under one contract
decisions.reason: ECC's full feature set is stable on Claude Code and minimal on Hermes; Hermes adds always-on chat, cron, persistent memory and any model provider
Hermes loads only the first matching context file and does not expand @ imports; generating keeps one source of truth

decisions.decision: Product LLM calls go through provider:model specs (anthropic: or hermes:)
decisions.reason: The request that agents should not be limited to Claude also applies to the in-app assistant, digest and CV parsing
